description: Use Garry Tan's exact Claude Code setup: 23 opinionated tools that serve as CEO, Designer, Eng Manager, Release Manager, Doc Engineer, and QA
summary: I like that gstack is just Markdown slash commands and a setup script — no proprietary runtime, no cloud lock-in — so you can read every role definition, fork the QA skill, and wire it into the session routing I already do in PenguPool without fighting a vendor. The concrete parts are what earn my trust: a QA skill that opens a real browser and reproduces a bug against your staging URL, a security skill that runs OWASP and STRIDE checks, a review skill that catches the bugs that pass CI but break in production. I'm less charmed by the "virtual engineering team" packaging and the sprint-counting, but the core insight — that a coding agent is more useful with a narrow role and a checklist than with a blank prompt — is the same direction I've been pushing in with AgentOn Pocket and PenguPool, and the fact that it's all local, all readable, MIT-licensed, makes it easy to trust.
